heading: Origami Crane — Tutorial Under Review
introduction: Our existing crane instructions are preserved below for reference. Read the review note before choosing a project.
durationNote: Planning estimate; allow extra time for your first attempt.
paper: One square sheet of thin origami paper, about 15 × 15 cm (6 × 6 in).

steps.title: Fold and Unfold Diagonally
steps.text: Fold your square paper in half diagonally, then unfold. Repeat along the other diagonal so both creases are visible.

steps.title: Fold in Half Both Ways
steps.text: Fold the paper in half horizontally and unfold, then vertically and unfold. You should now have four creases crossing in the center.

steps.title: Collapse into a Square Base
steps.text: Using the creases as guides, bring the corners together and collapse the paper into a smaller square shape.

steps.title: Fold Up the Sides
steps.text: Fold the left and right edges of the top layer inward to the center line, forming a kite shape. Repeat on the back.

steps.title: Petal Fold the Wings
steps.text: Lift each flap upward and flatten it into a petal fold to form the crane's wings on both sides.

steps.title: Shape the Head and Tail
steps.text: Fold one narrow point down slightly to create the head using a reverse fold, and leave the other as the tail.

steps.title: Your Crane is Complete!
steps.text: Gently pull the wings apart and curve them for a finished look. Add a fold to the head for a beak if you'd like.

tips: Line up corners before pressing a crease from the middle outwards.
Keep the paper facing the same way as the instruction before each fold.
commonMistakes: If layers do not line up, return to the last clear step rather than forcing the next fold.
Thick paper becomes difficult to fold as layers build up; try a larger, thinner square.

review.note: Desk review only; see docs/tutorial-audit-20261025.md. Physical fold test and owned step images required.
review.publicNote: The existing text compresses the square-base and petal-fold transitions and does not explain how to raise the neck and tail. There are no matching step images. We have not physically verified this sequence. Please use the illustrated resources below for a first attempt.
